prologue.title: Halloween, at last
prologue.narrator: Some nights, you think you're running toward a thrill. Sometimes, the thrill was waiting — still, patient.
prologue.text:
Your name is {{player}}, and you've been waiting for this moment for weeks.

Leo finally found a ladder to climb over the wall of Saint-Lunaire cemetery. Maya clutches her coat — and the bag of honey sweets she'd promised you for tonight. Sam is already filming everything on his phone. Inès packed three stories that are "actually scary."

The moon is full. Pumpkin lights still glow in the distance.

On the other side of the wall, the air is colder. The neighbourhood sounds feel far away.

Leo whispers as he jumps: "Come on, crew — let's make this a night to remember!"

Everyone laughs. You too. You feel alive, excited, ready to scream at the slightest noise.

Maya holds out the sweets. Her eyes linger on you a moment too long — then she smiles: "You'll get your share after the first scare, deal?"

choices.text: Be the first to dash toward the graves
Ask Inès to start with a story

legende.title: The tale of the fifth
legende.narrator: Legends told for laughs sometimes have a bad habit of remembering us.
legende.text:
Inès stops under a colonnade of trimmed yews.

"Know the legend? Every Halloween, a ghost joins a group of teens in a cemetery. It thinks it's part of the crew. It laughs, screams, plays dares…"

Maya shivers: "Great, thanks Inès."

"… and only at the end of the night does it understand that nobody could see it."

Maya looks down for a second.

Leo bursts out laughing: "Well luckily we're all here! Come on Sam, film Maya's face."

You slip between Maya and Leo, sticking out your tongue.

Maya jumps — looks you straight in the eyes — then bursts out laughing.

"Ah! You're impossible, {{player}}…" she murmurs.

Leo looks up: "What, what happened?"

Maya shakes her head: "Nothing. A root. Go on, take the photo, Sam."

"Nice," Sam says. "Let's keep going."

choices.text: Challenge them: dare to enter the mausoleum
Laugh with them to shake off the fear

defi.title: Truth or dare
defi.narrator: To dare is sometimes to walk where others still hesitate.
defi.text:
Leo pulls out an empty soda bottle — their summer "magic bottle," recycled for Halloween.

Truth or dare, cemetery edition. No backing out.

The bottle spins on a tilted slab. It stops facing you.

"{{player}}!" Maya shouts — **at you**, without hesitation. "Dare, obviously."

She winks at you. The others don't notice.

Leo whistles: "Dare to enter the Valmont mausoleum. First one through the door."

You step forward. An old lantern hangs on the rusted gate. You grab it — the metal is oddly cold.

Just then, a gust makes the mausoleum door creak on its own. The lantern flame lights in the same breath.

"Stylish," Sam says. "You've got a gift for atmosphere."

You push the door, smiling.

choices.text: Go in first, into the dark
Wait for the flame to steady

mausolee.title: The creaking door
mausolee.narrator: In the dark, the walls feel closer than they should.
mausolee.text:
The door creaks like an old laugh held back.

Inside smells of cold stone and dried wax. Names cover the walls: VALMONT, 1843–1921.

Leo whistles: "OK, that's creepy. We leaving?"

You slip behind Maya to scare her — breath in, shout, hand reaching for her shoulder…

Maya leaps, spins around, hands on her heart: "**Boo yourself!**"

The shout makes Leo and Sam jump. A slab tilts under Maya's foot — she wobbles, grabs the sarcophagus.

"Ow… damn, these slabs…" she says, laughing, **without looking away from you**.

Leo grins: "Good scare though." He means the slabs. Not you.

cabriole.title: Macabre hide-and-seek
cabriole.narrator: Among the stones, every sound becomes a dare.
cabriole.text:
Outside, the game resumes. Hide-and-seek among the stones: whoever surprises the loudest wins.

You hide behind a marble angel. Leo passes a metre away, looking for Maya.

"{{player}} must be on the other side," he says, running off.

You leap in front of him screaming — just as the nearby church bell strikes midnight. Leo startles, steps back… and slips on a dead leaf.

"Whoa!"

He catches himself on the angel: "… Damn, that bell. Fine, you win — where are you, {{player}}?"

He keeps searching elsewhere.

Across the alley, Maya saw you leap. She bites her lip to keep from laughing out loud.

Sam raises his phone: "Selfie of the night! Come on, squeeze in."

choices.text: Slip into the middle of the group
Watch the scene from your hiding spot

photo.title: The group photo
photo.narrator: A picture freezes a moment. Not always the one you think.
photo.text:
Sam counts: "One… two… three… smi—"

A burst of laughter all around. At the click, a gust of fog crosses the frame.

Maya never leaves the lens — she looks straight **at you**, a smile on her lips.

Sam turns the screen. Four clear faces: Leo, Maya, Inès, Sam. And an orange blur where you were standing.

"You moved, {{player}}," Sam says.

"No I didn't," you protest. "I was frozen."

Second shot — same timing: an owl takes off above you. Same blur for Sam.

Leo shrugs: "Must be the damp."

Inès looks down a darker alley: "We finish that way. Like usual."

choices.text: Follow them — the night goes on
Ask to see the photo up close

brume.title: The far alley
brume.narrator: When the night softens, it isn't always comforting.
brume.text:
Thin fog rises between the graves. The game gives way to a quieter walk.

Inès murmurs: "They say the dead walk tonight."

Maya: "Stop it, you're giving me goosebumps."

You walk with them, sure you're in the middle of the group.

You call out: "Maya!"

She turns — **at last** — and looks at you.

Her lips move. Nobody else seems to notice.

A branch snaps in the alley. Inès flinches. Maya keeps walking, voice low: "… We're almost there. You'll understand."

Inès, up ahead: "We're almost there."

You don't know where "there" is. You follow anyway.

tombe.title: Like every year
tombe.narrator: There comes a moment when the scare stops playing.
tombe.text:
They stop before a stone lighter than the others.

You read the carved name.

**{{player}}.** 2008–2025.

A Halloween date.

Maya sets the honey sweets at the foot of the stone — the ones she'd promised **for tonight**. She looks at you: "Like I promised."

Leo lights a candle, voice low: "… We did the neighbourhood. We came back here. Like always."

Sam: "We had fun. Well — we tried."

Inès stares at the stone: "We miss you."

Your name. Your date. Your sweets.

You open your mouth. No sound comes out.

It can't be. It can't be **you**.

choices.text: Read the stone again — and again

revelation.title: The fifth was you
revelation.narrator: The greatest twist isn't to scream. It's understanding who stayed with you all night.
revelation.text:
Then it all comes back — at once, like a tide.

You're the ghost. The night you fell from the wall. Every Halloween since, when the crew returns… you follow them, still believing the party starts again.

Leo can't see you. Neither can Sam. Neither can Inès.

**Maya can.**

She jumped **when you made a face** — not because of a root. In the mausoleum, it was **your** boo she heard. In the photo, she looked **straight at you**. When you called her name, she **turned around**.

Maya sees ghosts. And **every year**, she's the one who brings the others back here — to find you, {{player}}. To let you live a whole night with the crew again: the sweets, the dares, the laughter.

The others speak **about** you. Maya spoke **to** you — in secret, all evening long.

She sets the sweets at the foot of your stone. Leo wipes a tear: "OK. If {{player}} is here… knock over the candle."

Maya looks at you. Waits.

The flame wavers.

choices.text: Blow out the candle — one last scare for them
Stay still — and let the flame burn

fin_rideau.title: Boo, guys
fin_rideau.narrator: Sometimes the best scream is the one you feel on your neck — without ever knowing who it's from.
fin_rideau.text:
You blow.

The candle goes out — as a gust slams the cemetery gate shut in the distance. *Clang.*

Maya screams with the others — a little **too** loud, you can tell. Then she catches your eye: a smile. She **knew**.

Leo steps back, pale. Sam nearly drops his phone. Inès whispers: "… There."

"OK OK OK," Leo pants. "That wasn't funny. Well it was. Well… **{{player}}**?"

They run for the exit yelling, happy and terrified — exactly how you'd have wanted it.

Behind them, among the yews, Maya's laugh mingles with the wind. Or with you.

**END — The perfect scare**

fin_veille.title: Watching without getting in the way
fin_veille.narrator: Some ghosts scream. Others just keep the candle lit — even when nobody knows why it still burns.
fin_veille.text:
You don't blow.

The candle stays upright. Small, stubborn, as if shielded from a wind nobody feels.

Your friends leave at first light, eyes swollen. Maya turns once more: "See you next year, {{player}}. **I'll** bring the crew back."

She sees you. She'll return.

Among the yews, the fog lifts. The cemetery falls silent again — but not empty. **Inhabited**.

**END — Guardian of the cemetery**
